body:
Found earlier this session (Apple #13321/#13347): entity-graph's PublishObservation
(internal/entitygraph/observer.go) wrote straight to <timestamp-to-the-second>.json with no
collision check -- confirmed live, it silently clobbered a real founder directive ("24 more" blog
posts) that happened to land on the exact same second as one of entity-graph's own periodic
health-report observations. emily observe's own writer (internal/obs/writer.go) already had this
exact numeric-suffix collision guard, added 2026-08-09 after losing observations the same way --
entity-graph's independently-implemented writer never got the same fix.

Fixed: same collision-avoidance pattern (stat, bump to -2/-3/... suffix until a free name is
found), refactored PublishObservation into a thin wrapper over a new publishObservationAt(obs,
dir, ts) so the collision logic is directly unit-testable without depending on real wall-clock
timing. Two new regression tests (TestPublishObservation_DoesNotClobberSameSecondArchive,
TestPublishObservation_LatestJSONAlwaysReflectsMostRecentWrite) -- the first reproduces the exact
real failure and confirms both writes now survive under distinct filenames, the second confirms
latest.json (unlike the archive) is still correctly always-overwrite (that's its whole point,
unaffected by this fix).

go test ./... clean across the whole module. Rebuilt bin/entity-graph, restarted
fatbaby-entity-graph.service, confirmed healthy.
title: Fixed entity-graph observation-writer collision bug (real data loss, caught this session)
